title_en: The History of the Call to Islam in Mauritania
body_ar:
انتشر هذا الدين حتى وصل إلى كل أنحاء العالم، وكان الفضل في ذلك -بعد الله- للمجاهدين في سبيله من أهل العلم والفضل والصلاح. وقد فتح الفاتحون بلدان المغرب العربي، ثم تحللت هذه البلدان، وأصبحت دويلات متناحرة يأكل القوي منها الضعيف، فجاء الاستعمار وهي لقمة سائغة فابتلعها.
الله ناصر دينه:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم إن الحمد لله، نحمده ونستعينه، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا، ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له، ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، أرسله بالهدى ودين الحق بين يدي الساعة بشيراً ونذيراً، وداعياً إلى الله بإذنه وسراجاً منيراً. أما بعد: فإن خير الحديث كتاب الله، وخير الهدي هدي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وكل محدثة بدعة، وكل بدعة ضلالة، وكل ضلالة في النار. أيها الإخوة المؤمنون! السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته. إن هذا الدين دين الله، وليس دين الناس، فالله عز وجل ناصر دينه ومظهره ومعزه، بذل ذليل أو بعز عزيز...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* This religion spread until it reached every quarter of the world, and the credit for that — after God — belongs to those who strove in His path from among the people of knowledge, of merit and of righteousness. The conquerors opened the lands of the Arab Maghreb; then these lands came apart and became statelets at each other's throats, in which the strong devoured the weak — and so colonialism came upon it as an easy morsel, and swallowed it.

## God is the one who gives victory to His religion

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God. We praise Him and seek His help, and we take refuge with God from the evils of our own selves and from the ill of our deeds. Whomever God guides, none can lead astray; whomever He leads astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent with guidance and the religion of truth in advance of the Hour, as a bearer of good news and a warner, as one calling to God by His leave and as an illuminating lamp. To proceed: the best of speech is the Book of God, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, God bless him and grant him peace; and every newly introduced matter is an innovation in religion (bidʿah), and every innovation is an error, and every error is in the Fire.

Believing brothers! Peace be upon you, and God's mercy and His blessings. This religion is God's religion and not the religion of people. God, mighty and majestic, is the one who gives His religion victory, who makes it prevail and who gives it might — whether through the abasement of one abased or through the might of one mighty …

flags.context: the record breaks off and the full text sits behind a download
options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis at the end of the opening formula and the first sentence of the address, so that the history named in the title — the call to Islam in Mauritania — is never begun. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/g-20.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.context: the last clause before the text breaks off
options: whether through the abasement of one abased or through the might of one mighty
by the humiliation of the humiliated or the honour of the honoured
with the submission of the lowly or the strength of the strong
flags.note: The clause echoes the well-known report of Tamim al-Dari, that God will cause this religion to reach wherever night and day reach, 'بعز عزيز أو بذل ذليل'. The Sheikh gives it without attribution and with the two halves in the reverse of the usual order, so it has been rendered as prose in his own sentence and not marked as a quotation; no attribution and no grading has been supplied. Each half turns on a noun and its cognate adjective and the English keeps the figure.

flags.arabic: وكل محدثة بدعة، وكل بدعة ضلالة، وكل ضلالة في النار
flags.context: the opening formula of the address
options: every newly introduced matter is an innovation in religion (bidʿah), and every innovation is an error, and every error is in the Fire
every novelty is a heresy, every heresy is misguidance, and all misguidance is in Hell
flags.note: Part of the fixed opening formula of a sermon, quoted as formula rather than asserted as a ruling in this record. Two renderings must be avoided. 'بدعة' is fixed in the glossary as 'innovation in religion' and must not become 'heresy', which in English carries a doctrinal-trial sense Arabic does not; and 'ضلالة' is being led away from the right path, for which 'error' is flatter and safer than 'misguidance'. The formula is much quoted in contemporary polemic and an English page carrying it will be read in that light, so it is marked for editorial review even though nothing here applies it to anything.

flags.arabic: فجاء الاستعمار وهي لقمة سائغة فابتلعها
flags.context: the closing sentence of the site's synopsis
options: colonialism came upon it as an easy morsel, and swallowed it
the colonisers came when it was a mouthful easily swallowed, and swallowed it
flags.note: 'الاستعمار' is the abstract noun, colonialism or colonisation, not the colonisers; the English keeps the abstract as the grammatical subject, which is also what carries the image. Note that the pronoun 'وهي' is feminine singular and refers back to the lands collectively, not to any one state; the English 'it' keeps that.

'فتح' is the standard term for the early Islamic conquests and means literally an opening. English has no way to keep the figure and the event together, and 'conquerors opened' is a compromise that keeps both words visible. A reviewer may prefer 'conquered' twice; the choice has been left open rather than settled silently.

translator_notes: One of a run of nine records, IDs 725-733, in the Islamic-thought section, all uploaded on 10 May 2011 within about twenty minutes of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lecture, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/g-* series, numbered g-16 to g-24 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lecture was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

The transcribed portion is the long form of the khuṭbat al-ḥājah and one sentence of the address, and nothing else. This is precisely the case style guide section 9 describes: a sermon published as its opening formula.
The English breaks the transcribed portion into two paragraphs where the source runs on, separating the opening formula from the address to the audience. No word has been added or removed.
The record and record 730 carry the same upload timestamp in their aliases, 10 May 2011 at 10:32:27.
No ruling term from the five-rulings table appears anywhere in the record.
